guidelines: Each session is a short scripted interview on the snapshot: interviewer question, candidate answer, the interviewer's answer_summary for evaluate_answer, and the evidence examined before the answer.
Sessions mix accurate answers with answers that contradict the code at the pinned commit, so evaluations and reports have both strengths and discrepancies to describe.
The state is a hand-written plan in the shape planning writes. Evaluations and reports start from it, so re-recording the plan never invalidates them.
Line ranges refer to the snapshot bundle; refreshing the snapshot means re-checking them.

areas.name: Interview engine
areas.rationale: The voice interview depends on evaluate_answer and the other realtime tools returning quickly and safely.

areas.name: Interview reports
areas.rationale: The report job turns transcripts and evaluations into the candidate-facing report and must stay grounded in the repository.

areas.name: Interview planning
areas.rationale: Planning builds the coverage map and plan from repository memory and earlier interviews.

areas.name: Prompt and data safety
areas.rationale: Untrusted repository and transcript text reaches every model prompt.

plan.summary: StackPrep runs voice interviews about a candidate's own repository: Supabase edge functions serve the realtime interview tools, and Inngest jobs plan interviews, index code and write reports with OpenAI. The interview probes the evaluation tool, report grounding and planning.

phases.title: Reports
goals: Check how reports stay grounded and how the job handles model failures

phases.title: Live evaluation
goals: Probe the evaluation prompt and what happens when the model is slow

phases.title: Planning
goals: Explore plan normalization and the context sent to the planner

plan.opening_question: Walk me through what happens between an interview ending and the candidate seeing their report.

strategy.follow_up_style: Ask for the function involved and what happens when the model misbehaves.

sessions.description: Report answers: right about grounding and error classification, wrong that the report model sees discrepancy_detail.

turns.question: How does the report job stop the model from citing files the interview never touched?
turns.answer: groundReport filters repository_evidence: an entry survives only if its path was examined during the interview, cited in an evaluation's repo_evidence, or appears somewhere in repository memory. Then it re-parses the report with the schema and treats a mismatch as invalid output.
turns.answer_summary: Explains groundReport: repository_evidence entries are kept only for examined paths, evaluation repo_evidence or paths in memory, then the report is re-validated.

turns.question: What does the report model see about each evaluation?
turns.answer: buildReportInput hands it the whole evaluation row: the score, the rating, strengths, gaps, repo_evidence and the discrepancy_detail text, so the model can quote the exact contradiction.
turns.answer_summary: Claims buildReportInput passes each evaluation's score, rating, strengths, gaps, repo_evidence and discrepancy_detail to the report model.

turns.question: Which report failures does the job retry?
turns.answer: classifyReportError maps rate limits to a RetryAfterError using the provider's delay, retries unavailable and invalid output, except a refusal, which is non-retriable, and makes other request errors a non-retriable internal_error.
turns.answer_summary: Describes classifyReportError: rate limits retry after the provider delay, unavailable and invalid output retry, refusals and request errors are non-retriable.

sessions.description: Evaluation answers: right about the prompt and focus rules, wrong about a heuristic fallback on timeout.

turns.question: What goes into the prompt when evaluate_answer runs?
turns.answer: buildEvaluationInput fences six blocks: the plan summary and coverage areas, summary rows of repository memory within a budget, the examined evidence paths, the recent transcript, the current question and the interviewer's answer summary.
turns.answer_summary: Lists the fenced prompt blocks of buildEvaluationInput: plan and coverage, budgeted memory, examined evidence, recent transcript, question and answer summary.

turns.question: What happens if the evaluation model is slow or times out?
turns.answer: After the timeout evaluateAnswer falls back to a keyword heuristic that scores the answer against the coverage topics, so every answer still gets a rating.
turns.answer_summary: Claims evaluateAnswer falls back to a keyword heuristic score when the model times out.

turns.question: Could the guidance sent back to the voice model leak a score to the candidate?
turns.answer: The system prompt says focus is spoken guidance and must never include a score, rating or judgement, and the schema comment says the same. The focus text is also scrubbed and clipped before it goes back.
turns.answer_summary: Says the prompt and schema forbid scores in focus, and focus is scrubbed and clipped before returning.

sessions.description: Planning answers: right about normalizePlan and prior interviews, wrong that planner memory is unbounded.

turns.question: What does normalizePlan do to the model's output?
turns.answer: It rejects duplicate area ids, drops phase and focus references to unknown areas, removes phases that end up empty, resets every area to not_started and re-validates, throwing invalid output if the result no longer parses.
turns.answer_summary: Describes normalizePlan: duplicate ids rejected, unknown area references dropped, empty phases removed, statuses reset to not_started, result re-validated.

turns.question: Is there a limit on how much repository memory goes to the planner?
turns.answer: No, buildPlanningInput sends every memory row in full; the planning model has a big context window so there was no need for a limit.
turns.answer_summary: Claims buildPlanningInput sends all repository memory with no size limit.

turns.question: How do earlier interviews influence a new plan?
turns.answer: priorGuidance re-projects each earlier interview onto its number, status, coverage area statuses and per-category ratings, strengths and gaps, and that goes into a prior_interviews block so the planner can focus on gaps and avoid repeats.
turns.answer_summary: Explains that priorGuidance passes an allowlisted summary of earlier interviews into a prior_interviews block for the planner.
